results.title: Aircraft Pushback Explained: Tugs and Powerbacks | MiGFlug
results.content:
The ending is pure choreography: parking brake set, tug disconnected, headset unplugged, bypass pin shown to the cockpit, and a final signal before the jet taxis away under its own power.

A standard Boeing 737-800 pushback filmed on the ramp, from hook-up to disconnect.

## Towbarless tugs: lifting the nose off the ground

The alternative is the towbarless (TBL) tug. Instead of a bar, it clamps around the nose wheels and lifts them off the ground, so the tractor carries part of the aircraft's weight and steers it directly. There is no towbar to fetch, store or match to the aircraft type, and the shorter rig turns more precisely in tight corners. [...] Amsterdam Schiphol trialled TaxiBot in 2020 with Corendon Dutch Airlines, KLM, Transavia and easyJet. Schiphol's partners estimated savings of 50 to 85 per cent of the fuel normally burned while taxiing, because the engines still need time to warm up before take-off.

## Electric taxi: motors inside the wheels

The most radical answer puts the motor in the aircraft itself. Honeywell and Safran's Electric Green Taxiing System (EGTS) mounted electric motors in the inboard main wheels, powered by the auxiliary power unit's generator, so a jet could push back and taxi without its main engines. It was demonstrated on an Airbus A320 at the 2013 Paris Air Show. [...] The business case depended on expensive fuel. In July 2016 Honeywell walked away from the joint venture, citing low oil prices. Safran carried on alone, and Airbus withdrew its interest in 2019.

WheelTug, the other contender, replaces the nose wheels with units containing electric motors, again powered by the APU, and targets the Boeing 737NG. The FAA accepted its certification plan in December 2016, yet the promised service-entry dates have slipped again and again. In 2024 chief executive Isaiah Cox told The National he expected entry into service in 2026, with Spain's AlbaStar lined up as the first operator if certification went to plan.
